source_text: Τὰ γὰρ ἀεὶ καὶ δι᾿ ὅλου δίκαια καὶ πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην παρέχει ἐν παντὶ γένει ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἔστι πᾶν γένος γνωρίζον ὅτι μοιχεία κακὸν καὶ πορνεία καὶ ἀνδροφονία καὶ ὅσα ἄλλα τοιαῦτα. Κἂν πάντες πράττωσιν αὐτά, ἀλλ᾿ οὖν γε τοῦ ἐπίστασθαι ἀδικοῦντες, ὅταν πράττωσι ταῦτα, οὐκ ἀπηλλαγμένοι εἰσί, πλὴν ὅσοι ὑπὸ ἀκαθάρτου πνεύματος ἐμπεφορημένοι καὶ ἀνατροφῆς καὶ ἐθῶν φαύλων καὶ νόμων πονηρῶν διαφθαρέντες τὰς φυσικὰς ἐννοίας ἀπώλεσαν, μᾶλλον δὲ ἔσβεσαν ἢ ἐπεσχημένας ἔχουσιν. Ἰδεῖν γὰρ ἔστι καὶ τοὺς τοιούτους μὴ τὰ αὐτὰ παθεῖν βουλομένους ἅπερ αὐτοὶ τοὺς ἄλλους διατιθέασι. καὶ ἐν συνειδήσεσιν ἐχθραῖς ταῦτα ὀνειδίζοντας ἀλλήλοις ἅπερ ἐργάζονται. Ὅθεν μοι δοκεῖ καλῶς εἰρῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἡμετέρου κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐν δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην καὶ εὐσέβειαν πληροῦσθαι · εἰσὶ δὲ αὗται· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου, καὶ τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν . Ὁ γὰρ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος ἀγαπῶν τὸν θεόν, πλήρης θεοσεβοῦς γνώμης ὑπάρχων, οὐδένα ἄλλον τιμήσει θεόν· καὶ ἄγγελον ἐκεῖνον ἂν τιμήσει θεοῦ βουλομένου, τὸν ἀγαπώμενον ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ. Καὶ ὁ τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν ἀγαπῶν. ἅπερ ἑαυτῷ βούλεται ἀγαθά, κἀκείνῳ βουλήσεται· οὐδεὶς δὲ ἑαυτῷ κακὰ βουλήσεται. Ταὐτ᾿ οὖν τῷ πλησίον καὶ εὔξαιτ᾿ ἄν καὶ ἐργάσαιτο γενέσθαι, ἅπερ καὶ ἑαυτῷ, ὁ τὸν πλησίον ἀγαπῶν· πλησίον δὲ ἀνθρώπου οὐδὲν ἄλλο ἐστὶν ἢ τὸ ὁμοιοπαθὲς καὶ λογικὸν ζῶον, ὁ ἄνθρωπος. Διχῇ οὖν τῆς πάσης δικαιοσύνης τετμημένης, πρός τε θεὸν καὶ ἀνθρώπους, ὅστις, φησὶν ὁ λόγος, ἀγαπᾷ κύριον τὸν θεὸν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος, καὶ τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτόν [ibid.], δίκαιος ἀληθῶς ἂν εἴη. Ὑμεῖς δὲ οὔτε πρὸς θεὸν οὔτε πρὸς τοὺς προφήτας οὔτε πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς φιλίαν ἢ ἀγάπην ἔχοντες οὐδέποτε ἐδείχθητε, ἀλλ᾿, ὡς δείκνυται, καὶ εἰδωλολάτραι πάντοτε καὶ φονεῖς τῶν δικαίων εὑρίσκεσθε, ὡς καὶ μέχρις αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιβαλεῖν ὑμᾶς καὶ μέχρι νῦν ἐπιμένειν τῇ κακίᾳ ὑμῶν, καταρωμένους καὶ τῶν τοῦτον τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ὐφ᾿ ὑμῶν ἀποδεικνύντων εἶναι τὸν Χριστόν· καὶ πρὸς τούτοις ἐκεῖνον μὲν ὡς ἐχθρὸν θεοῦ καὶ κατηραμένον ἀξιοῦτε ἀποδεικνύναι ἐσταυρῶσθαι, ὅπερ τῆς ἀλογίστου ὑμῶν γνώμης ἔργον ἐστίν. Ἔχοντες γὰρ ἀφορμὰς ἀπὸ τῶν γενομένων σημείων διὰ Μωσέως συνιέναι ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν, οὐ βούλεσθε, ἀλλὰ καὶ πρὸς τούτοις, ἡμᾶς ἀλογεῖν δύνασθαι ὑπολαμβάνοντες, συζητεῖτε ὅπερ ὑμῖν συμβαίνει, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀπορεῖτε λόγων, ὅταν εὐτόνῳ τινὶ Χριστιανῷ συμβάλητε.
pass_a_gloss: For the things that are always and through all just and provide all righteousness in every kind of humans, and every kind knows that adultery is evil and fornication and murder and as many other such things. And even if all do these things, but yet they sin in knowing, when they do these things, they are not excused, except those who have been driven by an unclean spirit and corrupted by bad nurture and evil customs and laws, having destroyed the natural thoughts, or rather having extinguished them than having them disfigured. For it is possible to see even such people not wanting to suffer the same things that they impose on others. And in hostile consciences they reproach each other for the things they do. From which it seems to me to be well said by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, that all righteousness and piety are fulfilled in two commandments; and these are: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your strength, and your neighbor as yourself. For the one loving God with all his heart and with all his strength, being full of godly thought, will not honor any other god; and he will honor the angel who wishes to be honored by God, the one loved by the Lord and God. And the one loving his neighbor as himself, the things he wishes for himself, he will also wish for him; for no one wishes evil for himself. The same things, therefore, he who loves his neighbor would also pray for and do for him, as for himself; and neighbor of man is nothing else but the human, the like-feeling and rational living being. Thus, the whole righteousness is divided in two, towards God and towards humans, whoever, it says, loves the Lord God with all his heart and with all his strength, and his neighbor as himself, would truly be just. But you, having neither friendship nor love towards God nor towards the prophets nor towards yourselves, have never been shown, but, as is evident, you have always been found to be idolaters and murderers of the just, as also until the Christ you have laid hands on and until now you have persisted in your evil, cursing and denying those who demonstrate that the crucified one is the Christ; and besides these things, you consider him who was crucified by you to be an enemy of God and accursed, which is the work of your irrational thought. For having opportunities from the signs that happened through Moses to understand that he is the one, you do not want, but also, thinking that you can make us irrational, you dispute what happens to you, and you are at a loss for words when you encounter some Christian.
pass_b_english: The things that are always and everywhere just provide all righteousness for every kind of human being, and every kind knows that adultery is evil, as are fornication, murder, and all such things. Even if everyone does them, they still sin knowingly when they act, and they are not excused — except those who have been driven by an unclean spirit and corrupted by bad upbringing, evil customs, and wicked laws, who have destroyed their natural intuitions, or rather extinguished them than merely disfigured them. One can see even such people not wanting to suffer the very things they impose on others. And in hostile consciences they reproach each other for the deeds they themselves commit. From this it seems to me that our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ spoke well when he said that all righteousness and piety are fulfilled in two commandments (Matthew 22:37-40): You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your strength, and your neighbor as yourself (Leviticus 19:18). The one who loves God with all his heart and strength, being full of godly purpose, will not honor any other god; he will even honor the angel whom God wishes to honor, the one beloved by the Lord and God. And the one who loves his neighbor as himself will wish for that neighbor the same good things he wishes for himself, for no one wishes evil for himself. Therefore, the one who loves his neighbor will both pray for and work to bring about for his neighbor the same things he desires for himself; for a neighbor of a human being is nothing else but the human — the like-feeling, rational living being, the human. Thus the whole of righteousness, divided in two toward God and toward humans, means that whoever, as the Word says, loves the Lord God with all his heart and all his strength, and his neighbor as himself, would truly be just. But you have never been shown to have either friendship or love toward God, or toward the prophets, or even toward yourselves; instead, as is evident, you have always been found to be idolaters and murderers of the just — so much so that you laid hands on the Christ himself, and to this day you persist in your evil, cursing and denying those who demonstrate that this crucified one is the Christ. Moreover, you demand that he be proven to be an enemy of God and accursed, worthy of crucifixion — which is the work of your irrational mind. For though you have had opportunities from the signs performed through Moses to understand that he is the one, you do not want to; and besides, thinking you can make us irrational, you dispute what happens to you, and you are left without words when you encounter a coherent Christian.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly incorporates the required scripture citations (Matthew 22:37-40 and Leviticus 19:18) for the commandments quoted in the text. The distinction between 'extinguished' (ἔσβεσαν) and 'disfigured' (ἐσχημασμένας) is preserved. The translation of 'ἀλογίστου' as 'irrational'/'irrational mind' is consistent.
